messages:
Maria: hey folks, quick heads up — the ruby sample app onboarding is tripping new users when bundler binstubs are present. repro: `bundle install --binstubs` then `bin/ruby sample_app.rb` -> 401 Unauthorized. anyone seen this?
Kevin: can you paste the minimal error you get?
Maria: sure — it just prints "Unauthorized: missing Authorization header" from the sdk call. our quickstart expects REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or a refresh flow, but binstubs seem to run without loading the dev `.env` in a couple of setups. repro snippet:
```
$ bundle install --binstubs
$ bin/ruby sample_app.rb
=> 401 Unauthorized
```
SamCI: saw a failure that looks similar in the matrix job earlier (ruby-quickstart, job 12). link: https://ci.internal/ci/xyz/job/12 :facepalm:
Julia: hmm — we're currently suggesting `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` in the README but not surfacing a clear error. can we detect missing auth and print an actionable message?
Kevin: proposed tiny fix: in sample_app bootstrap, detect empty header and raise `Please set REDWOOD_API_KEY or run with bundle exec / ensure binstub env loads`. will open a PR with that plus a README note. also add a fallback check for `~/.config/redwood/token.json` for local dev.
PR-Bot: opened #2346 by kevin: "ruby sampleapp: improve auth messaging + binstub compatibility"
Maria: awesome. can you also mention `bundle exec ruby sample_app.rb` as a workaround? some newbies only run `bin/ruby` and miss env vars.
Kevin: yep added both suggestions, plus a unit test that simulates `ENV` unset and ensures the error message includes actionable steps.
SamCI: re-ran the flaky job, job 12 re-run passed :tada:
Julia: I'll add a short note in the onboarding checklist and ping the docs team for a small quickstart tweak.
Maria: thanks all — leaving a short post in #docs and will follow up after the PR lands. :thumbsup:
